label: Appearance
value: Anne has a slender build.

Her red hair is her greatest source of personal trouble until she accidentally dyes it green and has to have it shaved short. As she grows taller, she shoots up rapidly and eventually surpasses Marilla in height.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables.
unit: Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables as an eleven-year-old orphan due to a mistake, as Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert intended to adopt a boy. Despite initial doubts, Marilla and Matthew decide to keep her. Anne settles into Avonlea, forming a passionate friendship with Diana Barry and entering school, where she breaks her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head after he calls her "Carrots." Following a series of mishaps—including accidentally intoxicating Diana with currant wine, dyeing her hair green, and getting stranded on a bridge while playing Elaine—Anne repeatedly proves her heart and courage. She saves Minnie May Barry's life during a case of croup, wins back Mrs. Barry's favor, and earns the devotion of the town. Under the guidance of her teacher Miss Stacy, Anne excels academically, entering Queen's Academy where she wins the prestigious Avery Scholarship. Following Matthew's sudden death and the threat of Marilla losing her eyesight, Anne gives up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables as the local schoolteacher, finally forgiving Gilbert Blythe and establishing a close friendship with him.

label: History
value: Billy lives in Avonlea
unit: Billy lived in Avonlea with his family. When a concert was held at the White Sands Hotel, he drove his sister Jane, Anne Shirley, and Diana Barry over in his family's double-seated buggy. He insisted that Anne sit on the front seat with him because he greatly admired her. During the drive, he grinned and chuckled at Anne's civilities, unable to think of replies in time. After the concert, he decamped to avoid being invited to supper with the performers, but he waited with the horse team to drive the girls home safely under the moonlight.

He insisted that Anne sit on the front seat with him because he greatly admired her. During the drive, he grinned and chuckled at Anne's civilities, unable to think of replies in time. After the concert, he decamped to avoid being invited to supper with the performers, but he waited with the horse team to drive the girls home safely under the moonlight.

label: History
value: Diana returned to Orchard Slope
unit: Diana returned to Orchard Slope after visiting her aunt in Carmody and met Anne Shirley, pledging to be her lifelong bosom friend. After accidentally drinking currant wine at Green Gables thinking it was raspberry cordial, Diana became intoxicated, leading her mother to forbid her from playing with Anne. The ban was lifted when Anne saved Diana's younger sister Minnie May from a severe case of croup. Later, while attending a Debating Club concert and staying overnight in the Barry spare room, Diana and Anne accidentally jumped into bed on visiting Great-Aunt Josephine Barry. Diana subsequently joined Anne's story club, went on a trip to the Charlottetown Exhibition, and continued her close friendship with Anne even after she did not join the Queen's preparation class.

label: History
value: Gilbert returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert returned to Avonlea after spending time in Alberta and visiting relatives in New Brunswick. On his first day back at school, he attempted to capture Anne Shirley's attention by pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots,' which resulted in Anne smashing her slate over his head. Although Gilbert publicly took the blame and apologized, Anne held a bitter grudge against him. During their time at school, a fierce academic rivalry developed between them, leading them both to pass the entrance examinations for Queen's Academy with tied top scores. At Queen's, Gilbert pursued the First Class teacher's license and was awarded the medal for academic excellence. Learning that his father could not afford to send him to college, he initially accepted the teaching position at the Avonlea school. However, upon hearing that Anne needed to stay close to Green Gables, he generously withdrew his application so she could teach in Avonlea instead, securing a position for himself at White Sands. Anne thanked him for his sacrifice, and the two finally resolved their long-standing feud and became close friends.

On his first day back at school, he attempted to capture Anne Shirley's attention by pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots,' which resulted in Anne smashing her slate over his head. Although Gilbert publicly took the blame and apologized, Anne held a bitter grudge against him. During their time at school, a fierce academic rivalry developed between them, leading them both to pass the entrance examinations for Queen's Academy with tied top scores. At Queen's, Gilbert pursued the First Class teacher's license and was awarded the medal for academic excellence. Learning that his father could not afford to send him to college, he initially accepted the teaching position at the Avonlea school. However, upon hearing that Anne needed to stay close to Green Gables, he generously withdrew his application so she could teach in Avonlea instead, securing a position for himself at White Sands. Anne thanked him for his sacrifice, and the two finally resolved their long-standing feud and became close friends.

label: History
value: Jane is a schoolgirl in Avonlea.
unit: Jane is one of the schoolgirls in Avonlea who becomes close friends with Anne Shirley. She participates in school activities, Sunday-school picnics, the story club, and dramatic enactments with her friends. When the Queen's class is formed, Jane joins to prepare for a teaching career, stating she intends to devote her life to teaching rather than marriage. She passes the Entrance examination, attends Queen's Academy, and excels in the domestic science course. After graduating with her teacher's license, she is offered a teaching position at the Newbridge school.

She joined the Queen's class organized by Miss Stacy and successfully passed the Entrance exam to Queen's Academy, where she took up Second Class teacher's course work. At Queen's, she achieved preeminence as the sharpest-tongued student in attendance. After graduating from her first year at Queen's, she decided to return to the academy for another year rather than teach.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with her brother Matthew, maintaining a quiet and exceptionally orderly routine. Deciding to adopt an orphan boy to help Matthew with farm work, they sent word through acquaintances, but were shocked when Anne Shirley arrived instead. Though initially determined to return Anne to the asylum, Marilla relented out of compassion and Matthew's quiet persistent desire to keep her. She took on the duty of raising Anne, enforcing strict discipline and practical moral lessons while gradually growing deeply attached to the imaginative girl. Over the years, Marilla supported Anne's education, witnessed her triumphs at school, and slowly grew softer and more expressive in her affection. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack caused by financial ruin, Marilla faced failing eyesight and considered selling Green Gables. However, Anne decided to stay home and teach locally to assist her, enabling Marilla to preserve their beloved home.

value: Matthew is extremely shy.
unit: Extremely shy, quiet, and silent, Matthew hated going among strangers or places where he had to speak. He stood in great dread of women and little girls, believing they secretly laughed at him, though he felt comfortable with his sister Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Despite his bashfulness, he possessed a gentle, sympathetic heart and a quiet, stubborn persistency when he took a whim into his head.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert went to the Bright River station.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert went to the Bright River station to pick up an orphan boy intended to help him with farm labor, only to find Anne Shirley waiting instead. Touched by her enthusiasm, he brought her home to Green Gables and quietly insisted to his sister Marilla that they keep her. Over the next three years, he formed a deep bond of friendship with Anne, acting as a gentle confidant who indulged her wish for fashionable puff-sleeved dresses and supported her ambitions. Suffering from heart trouble, Matthew continued to work hard on the farm alongside hired help. Shortly after Anne's return from Queen's Academy, news of the sudden collapse of the Abbey Bank—where all the Cuthberts' savings were kept—caused him to suffer a fatal heart attack on the doorstep of Green Gables.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips is the schoolmaster at Avonlea.
unit: As the schoolmaster at Avonlea, Mr. Phillips devoted much of his time and attention during lessons to Prissy Andrews, sitting in the back to explain her studies or write notes on her slate. During class, he punished Anne Shirley for losing her temper by making her stand on the platform by the blackboard and writing a message above her head that spelled her name without an 'e'. The next day, after a group of tardy pupils returned late from picking gum, he used Anne as a scapegoat and forced her to sit beside Gilbert Blythe as punishment. Later in the school year, he gave a heart-stirring recitation of Mark Antony's oration over Cæsar at the local concert. At the end of June, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to the students before concluding his term as Avonlea's schoolmaster.

During class, he punished Anne Shirley for losing her temper by making her stand on the platform by the blackboard and writing a message above her head that spelled her name without an 'e'. The next day, after a group of tardy pupils returned late from picking gum, he used Anne as a scapegoat and forced her to sit beside Gilbert Blythe as punishment. Later in the school year, he gave a heart-stirring recitation of Mark Antony's oration over Cæsar at the local concert. At the end of June, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to the students before concluding his term as Avonlea's schoolmaster.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel is a capable housewife.
unit: Mrs. Rachel is a capable, notable housewife and energetic church worker who prides herself on managing both her own affairs and those of her neighbors. Observant and intensely curious, she keeps a sharp eye on everything in Avonlea and never hesitates to speak her mind with outspoken directness. Though officious, pessimistic, and prone to meddling, she possesses a kindly heart, readily admits her mistakes when proven wrong, and is widely recognized as a dependable, hard-working Christian woman.

unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde observed Matthew Cuthbert unexpectedly driving out in formal clothes, which led her to visit Green Gables and learn that he and Marilla were adopting an orphan boy from Nova Scotia. Upon meeting the adopted orphan, Anne Shirley, she bluntly criticized her appearance and sparked a furious outburst from the child. After Anne apologized at Marilla's insistence, Mrs. Rachel readily forgave her and gifted her flowers. Over time, she kept a watchful eye on Anne's upbringing, advising Marilla on school matters and dress choices, including sewing Anne's first dress with fashionably puffed sleeves. She actively participated in community events, attending political rallies and helping organize Sunday-school picnics. Although initially doubtful about Anne's adoption and her higher education pursuits, Mrs. Rachel eventually acknowledged her mistake, growing very fond of Anne and admiring her transformation into a steady, reliable, and pretty young woman.

label: History
value: Ruby attends Avonlea School
unit: Ruby attends Avonlea School under Mr. Phillips, where she frequently witnesses or gets involved in schoolroom drama, including being accidentally pinned to her seat by Gilbert Blythe. She joins the local story club organized by Anne Shirley, though her story contributions tend to be overly sentimental. After Miss Stacy takes over as teacher, Ruby joins the Queen's Academy preparation class and participates in school concerts and recitations. She passes the Entrance Examinations for Queen's Academy and moves to town to pursue her studies. During her time at Queen's, she is recognized as the handsomest girl in her year and often walks with Gilbert Blythe. Upon obtaining her teacher's license, she secures a teaching position at a school up west.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired as Avonlea school's first female teacher. She quickly won the hearts of her pupils by introducing engaging methods like physical culture exercises, recitation Fridays, and field afternoons for nature study. In November, she organized a Christmas concert with her students to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. She later formed an advanced class to prepare interested students for the Queen's Academy entrance examination. Although offered a teaching role in her home district, she chose to stay in Avonlea to see her students through their preparations. At the end of the term, she advised her students on how to prepare for the exams, personally accompanying them to the Academy on their test day. Her entire Queen's class successfully passed their entrance examinations.
